name: CI review as a GitHub App

pr.title: Post CI reviews as a GitHub App, and post Projector's own as Projector Review
pr.head: c9c37252d8bb679df71a0352652830f044653737

summary: Projector can review a pull request in a GitHub Actions job with no agent session running. The job runs project review run through the reusable action in actions/review/. Until now, those reviews posted with the workflow's own token, so they appeared as github-actions[bot]. Any workflow in the repository can post as that account, and the name says nothing about Projector.

This change lets the reviews post as a GitHub App, an account a person registers once and installs on their repositories. The action gains an app-id input. When it is set, a new step uses the app's private key to mint a short-lived installation token, and the review posts as <slug>[bot] with that token. project init --ci-review --ci-app <slug> writes the setup, and Projector's own workflow switches to its projector-review app.

• Left for later: context repositories, the other feature an app token enables, stay deferred.
  • Unchanged: the summary job keeps the workflow's token, because it pushes refs/projector/summaries and the app token is read-only for contents.
  • The review found one open finding: the private key stays in the environment of the action steps that run after the agent. The flag on actions/review/action.yml explains it.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• App slug: the URL name of a GitHub App, such as projector-review. The app posts as <slug>[bot].
  • Installation token: a token GitHub issues to an app for the accounts it is installed on. It lasts an hour.
  • Composite action: an action made of steps, like actions/review/action.yml. The caller's env reaches every one of its steps.
  • review.reviewers: the logins whose Projector verdicts count beside the repository's own accounts.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One review at c9c3725: changes requested, with one P2 finding on the key's exposure and one suggestion.
  • CI check and the repository's review.gate steps passed on this head.

groups.title: The action mints the app's token
groups.kicker: How a review job gets an app token and posts with it
intro: The reusable action actions/review/action.yml runs every CI review. With an app-id input, a new step, Mint the app's token, calls actions/create-github-app-token. It reads the private key from the PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY environment variable the caller sets. The token it mints reaches only the job's repository, with the same permissions the workflow grants its own token.

The review step then uses that token as GH_TOKEN and names <slug>[bot] as PROJECTOR_TOKEN_LOGIN. It falls back to github.token and github-actions[bot] when no app is set. The steps that install and run the agent set the key variable to an empty string, so those processes do not get it.

files.note: Adds the app-id input and the mint step, and switches the review step's token and login to the app's.

checks.text: Only the install and review steps blank PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY. Save the review state and Hand the summary to the summary job run after them and still get the key in their environment. So code that the agent or an install script leaves behind, such as a loader variable written to $GITHUB_ENV, can read it there. The review asks for an app-private-key input instead, because a composite action's inputs reach no step's environment.
The token and the login both come from the app step's outputs, so the review never posts as one account while naming another.

files.note: Tests the app workflow text, the key blanking in the install and review steps, the token and login wiring, and how init handles an app.

groups.title: init and ci-workflow write the app into the workflow
groups.kicker: The CLI flags, the workflow template, and the setting
intro: project init --ci-review --ci-app <slug> looks the app's numeric ID up with gh api apps/<slug>. It refuses an app GitHub does not show before it writes anything. It writes the ID into the workflow as app-id, adds PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY to the step's secrets, and records review.ci_app, so a later init rebuilds the same workflow. project review ci-workflow --app <slug> prints that same file.

init also puts <slug>[bot] in review.reviewers in place of github-actions[bot], so a workflow posting with its own token no longer counts as a reviewer. At a terminal, it asks for the path of the key file and has gh secret set read it as standard input, so the key never appears on a command line.

files.note: Adds --ci-app and --app, app_id for the lookup, the reviewers rewrite, and set_app_key for the secret.

checks.text: This line drops only github-actions[bot]. A switch from one app to another leaves the old <slug>[bot] counted, which the review lists as a suggestion.

app_id raises on a 404 or a non-numeric answer, and init turns that into an error before it writes the workflow or records any setting. test_an_app_github_does_not_show_is_refused_before_anything_is_written covers it, and it passed on this head.

files.note: workflow_text takes an optional app ID and fills the template's @APP@ slot and the extra secret.
Adds the @APP@ slot before the review step's env:. With no app, it expands to nothing.

groups.title: Projector's own reviews post as Projector Review
intro: Projector's workflow passes app-id: '5827721' for the projector-review app and the key secret. .projector.toml records the app and counts only projector-review[bot] as an extra reviewer. Because a writer's pull request runs the action from its own checkout, any writer of this repository could reach the key, so the app stays installed only on the owner's repositories.

files.note: Passes the app ID and the key secret to the action.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: How to set an app up, and what the plan records
intro: docs/review-in-ci.md gains a Post as a GitHub App section and a row for the app-id input. docs/cli.md describes the new flags and the review.ci_app setting. The plan's § 9 records that the app input shipped before context repositories, and how Projector's own reviews post.
